region.text: Malaya, the core of the federation: 'Proclamation of Malaysia: 16 September 1963'

ledger.note: 1963: Malaysia is proclaimed (16 September): 'independent Malaya united with the then British crown colonies of North Borneo, Sarawak, and Singapore'. The date had been moved from 31 August 1963 after a UN survey was asked for 'by opponents of the federation such as Indonesia's Sukarno and the Sarawak United Peoples' Party'.
1963: Singapore joins Malaysia as a state (16 September).

region.text: the crown colony of Sarawak, with Limbang (annexed by Rajah Charles Brooke on 17 March 1890)

ledger.note: 1963: Sarawak joins Malaysia (16 September). The Limbang page adds that Brunei's Sultans made claims to Limbang 'in 1951, 1963, and 1973'.

region.text: the crown colony of North Borneo (Sabah)

ledger.note: 1963: North Borneo joins Malaysia (16 September) and becomes Sabah. The Philippines 'has a dormant claim to the eastern part of Sabah' (infobox page).

region.text: Singapore: 'Singapore became a sovereign state on 9 August'

ledger.note: 9 August 1965: Singapore leaves Malaysia. 'The Separation Agreement was signed on 7 August 1965'; the Constitution and Malaysia (Singapore Amendment) Bill 1965 'passed unanimously by a vote of 126-0 without PAP representatives present'. The Malaysia page says only 'In August 1965, Singapore was separated from the federation'.

wars.name: Indonesia-Malaysia confrontation
wars.outcome: 'A final peace agreement was signed on 11 August 1966 with Indonesia formally recognising Malaysia.' The infobox gives 20 January 1963 to 11 August 1966 and no territorial change.
wars.note: The page describes no land held by Indonesian forces: Indonesian-trained raiders seized the Tebedu police station (12 April 1963, 'about 64km from Kuching and 3.2km from the border') and attacked Gumbang; a seaborne force landed at Pontian on 17 August 1964 and paratroops near Labis on 2-3 September 1964; British 'Claret' cross-border raids went to 3,000, then 6,000 and, 'after the Battle of Plaman Mapu in April 1965', 10,000 yards into Kalimantan. So there are no contest events and no zone. The Brunei revolt of 8 December 1962 (the TNKU occupied Limbang, contained 'within five days') precedes the state.

certainty.note: The land frontiers follow colonial boundaries and the Johor Strait; the Philippines' dormant claim to eastern Sabah, the disputed maritime boundaries, the Spratly claims and Brunei's Limbang claim ('the dispute ended in 2009' on the maritime boundaries; the land boundary with Brunei was still not fully demarcated in 2023, per the Limbang page) leave those edges approximate.

notes: Six pages were opened against a budget of five (the Limbang Division page was thin and replaced by the Limbang article; the Federation of Malaya and Singapore in Malaysia pages are shared with the federation-of-malaya and republic-of-singapore dossiers). Cliopatria problems: (1) Singapore is kept inside Malaysia through 1966 although it left on 9 August 1965, and its own row starts in 1967 (new keyframe malaysia_1965); (2) the shapes before 1987 omit two border cells at Limbang (506 km2; Limbang was annexed by Sarawak in 1890, and one of the two cells lies on the Brunei side in Natural Earth), which the British Colonial Empire row draws until 1986: keyframes 1963 and 1967 are adjusted by adding them back; the gazetteer has no name for Limbang (listed under gazetteer_names_needed). The Federation of Malaya (to 1963) is a different Cliopatria row and its own dossier; the federation was 'reconstituted as Malaysia' so a gap-filler may prefer a rename. The Brunei revolt of December 1962, Brunei's refusal to join, the Cobbold Commission and the Malaysia Agreement of July 1963 are not on the Malaysia page. Labuan became a federal territory in 1984 and Putrajaya an administrative centre (no year on the page); neither moves a border. Ligitan and Sipadan (2002) and Pedra Branca (2008) are conf-1 events recorded from the researcher's memory because the pages are silent; they are off the land grid. The Philippines' dormant claim to eastern Sabah and the Spratly claims (Swallow Reef is not named on the page) are not territorial events. The Malayan Emergency belongs to the federation-of-malaya dossier. Reviewer se-04-b (2026-10-20): the 2002 gain of Ligitan and Sipadan from Indonesia and the 2008 loss of Pedra Branca to Singapore were removed from the ledger: no land changed hands. The International Court of Justice found on 17 December 2002 that 'sovereignty over the islands of Ligitan and Sipadan belongs to Malaysia', on 'the effectivites principle' (Malaysia and the British before it held and developed them; Indonesia's claim dates from 1969), and on 23 May 2008 that 'sovereignty over Pedra Branca belongs to Singapore' and 'sovereignty over Middle Rocks belongs to Malaysia' (Singapore and the United Kingdom before it had administered Pedra Branca since Horsburgh Lighthouse was built in 1850-1851; Malaysia's claim began with its map of 21 December 1979). Pages: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligitan_and_Sipadan_dispute and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedra_Branca_dispute.
